title: The Night the Sea Breathed Out
blurb: The sea has gone out farther than anyone in Kettle Cove remembers, and young salvager Tamsin Vey keeps hearing a bell beneath the water.
recap: The sea went out in the night, farther than anyone in Kettle Cove could remember. Tamsin Vey took up her gaff hook, learned Brine Lash from old Ama Brack, and chased a giant crab out of Cobb's boat. On the bare sand she found a carved stone, a Tide Seal of drowned Marrow, and it cracked under her hand. A bell rang beneath the seabed, and a voice she almost knew said: come down.

entities.text: KETTLE COVE. Mind the cliff. Mind the sea. Mind your manners. (Somebody has scratched in: MIND THE CRABS.)
Your cottage. The kettle's cold; you left in a hurry.
Ama's tide-house. Almanacs are stacked to the rafters, and every one of them is wrong about tonight.
Mags's house. A note on the door says: AT THE STALL, OBVIOUSLY.
Nell and Bo's house. It smells of fish stew and wet dog.

pro_start: The night the sea breathed out, nobody in Kettle Cove slept.
The water didn't crash or roar. It just... left. It pulled back past the reef, past the bell buoy, past anything anyone had a name for.

pro_start.t: ...There it is again. That sound. Like a bell ringing under the water.
Ama will be up. She's always up when the sea does something strange. She'll be at the cliff edge, east of the village.

ama_1.t: There you are, {name}. Come and look. Three hundred paces of seabed, bare as a plate.
My grandmother's grandmother never saw the tide go out this far. Seventy years I've read this water, and it's never once surprised me. Until tonight.

ama_bell.t: I thought it was my old ears. A bell, under the water. The old songs say Marrow had a bell as big as a house.
Marrow? The drowned kingdom from the bedtime stories?
Bedtime stories have to start somewhere.

ama_danger.t: Danger? The sea's gone, child. There's nothing left to drown in.
It's what comes back that worries me.

ama_1b.t: Fetch your gaff hook from the net shed by your cottage. Then go down to the beach and check on Cobb. That boy took his boat down to the slipway before dawn and I haven't seen him since.
And {name}? If the flats are crawling with things that used to live under the water, mind your step. At low tide a blade finds the gaps. At high tide the sea fights for whoever calls it.
Breathe out slow, push with your whole chest, and the brine follows your hand. Your mother did it without thinking. You've watched me do it a hundred times. Go on. Show me.

ama_1b: You breathe out, slow, and push. A rope of seawater lifts out of a rock pool and cracks like a whip.

ama_1b.t: There. Brine Lash. It costs breath, so don't waste it. Now go: hook, then Cobb.

ama_2.t: Gaff hook from the net shed, then Cobb at the slipway. The path down the cliff is in the middle of the village. Off you go.

ama_3.t: Ama! There's a stone out on the sand. Round, carved, glowing. When I touched it I heard the bell, and a voice.
It said my name. And then it said 'come down'.

ama_3: Ama looks out at the bare seabed for a long time.

ama_3.t: That's a Tide Seal. My grandmother drew them in the margins of her almanacs. Seven seals, the old song goes, to hold the sea above Marrow.
If one of them has cracked, then the sea isn't leaving us, {name}.

got_gaff.t: My old gaff hook. Salt-pitted, but the point's still sharp. (Equipped: Attack +2.)

cobb_1.t: {name}! Don't come any closer! There's a crab in my boat. A crab the size of a cartwheel!
Have you got your hook? Don't go at it bare-handed, it's already had my boot!

cobb_fight.t: You've got your hook! Get it out of there, please. Gently. Or not gently. Whatever works!

do.intro: The brinecrab clacks out of Cobb's boat!

cobb_fight.t: You did it! I'd hug you but I smell like crab.
Look, out on the wet sand, right in the middle of the bay. Something's glowing. It wasn't there yesterday, because yesterday it was under twenty feet of water.

cobb_after.t: That glowing thing on the wet sand, south of here. Go and look! I'm not going near it. I've had enough surprises for one morning.

cobb_p1.t: {name}, you're going out on the flats? Can you do me a favour?
I set my crab trap right at the old waterline last night, and now it's halfway to the horizon. My gran made that trap. Look for it on the east side of the flats, near the coral.

cobb_trap.t: Here. I found this sea-glass on the dock this morning. It's not much, but it's green, and green's lucky.

cobb_done.t: Gran's trap is back on its hook. If you see any more of those giant crabs out there, tell them Cobb says sorry about the boot.

mags.t: Shop's open, sea or no sea. People still need feeding, and they still need patching up.
Come back alive, love. Dead customers never pay their tabs.

nell_1.t: The well bucket came up full of sand this morning. Sand! From a well! I've half a mind to write a letter to someone. Who do you write to about the sea?

nell_2.t: Bo wants to walk out on the flats and 'find treasure'. I told him the only treasure out there is a twisted ankle. Then I saw you go, and now he won't stop asking.

hob_1.t: Forty years I've mended nets in this cove. I've never once had to mend one because the sea ran off and left it lying in the sun.

hob_2.t: You're going out there? Then take some advice: keep the cliffs at your back and the basins in your pocket. Rest at the old stone basins whenever you see one. Folk say the sea remembers you there.

bo.t: Is the sea coming back? Mum says it's coming back. Is it?

go.t: Phew. I left my boat out there.
...That's what grown-ups say when it's bad.

then: Cobb's boat sits high and dry on its keel, with a crab-shaped dent in the bench.
else: Something is clacking around inside Cobb's boat.

seal1_early: A round stone half-buried in the wet sand, carved with lines that glow faintly. You should check on Cobb first. Somebody's yelling on the beach.
seal1: A round stone of grey Marrow granite, half-buried in the sand. Lines are carved deep into it, and they glow like sea-fire.
As you kneel beside it, a crack runs across its face with a sound like ice on a pond.
BOOM. The bell. Not in your ears this time. In your ribs.

seal1.t: That voice... I know that voice.
Ama needs to see this. She's still up on the cliff.

seal1_after: The Tide Seal lies cracked in two. The glow inside it has gone out, like a lamp someone forgot to refill.

noflats.t: Not yet. Something's happened, and Ama will want to hear about it first.

cliffview: From the foot of the cliff path the whole bay lies open: wet sand, rock pools, stranded kelp, and far out, a straight grey line running south. A road?

q_pro.title: The Long Low Tide
q_pro.desc: The sea went out in the night, farther than anyone remembers. Find out why.

steps.text: Find Ama at the cliff edge, east of the village.
Take your gaff hook from the net shed by your cottage.
Help Cobb at the slipway down on the beach.
Look at the glowing stone on the wet sand.
